sherlock-holmes.traps: Disguises: (1) the ‘drunken-looking groom’ at 121 is Holmes — Watson recognises him within the same paragraph; leave ‘groom’ unbound (121, and 126 ‘a groom out of work’). M 121 already names Holmes (‘certain it was Holmes’) where O says ‘it was indeed he’. Holmes is the unnamed groom who witnesses the wedding (137–141) — narrated by Holmes himself, not concealed. (2) the ‘amiable and simple-minded Nonconformist clergyman’ at 170 is Holmes, shown openly to the reader; Irene’s ‘dear, kind old clergyman’ (242) is also Holmes. Do NOT bind ‘clergyman’ to Holmes globally: ‘surpliced clergyman’/‘the clergyman’ at 137/141 is the real officiating clergyman (st-monicas-clergyman). (3) The injured man at 185–193 (‘the poor gentleman’, ‘He is dead’, ‘a brave fellow’) is Holmes faking injury with red paint (revealed 202) — leave unbound. (4) ‘a slim youth in an ulster’ (213) who greets ‘Mister Sherlock Holmes’ is NOT Holmes — it is Irene (gated 243). (5) ‘Bohemian soul’ (1) is an adjective about Holmes, not Bohemia’s King. ‘my dear sir’ (249) is the King to Holmes — unbound.
